cards.name: Bitmap Mask
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Bitmap Mask docker (the bitmap color mask, also under Window > Dockers > Effects). In the docker you pick colors from a selected bitmap and either hide those colors (they become transparent) or show only them, with a tolerance slider deciding how close a pixel must be to match.
cards.how: Select a bitmap, open the docker, pick colors with the eyedropper (or edit a swatch), set the tolerance slider (0-100) for each, choose Hide selected or Show selected, then Apply. Masks can be saved and reloaded from the docker.
use_for: dropping a flat white or solid-color background out of a product shot or scanned logo
knocking a single color out of a scanned stamp, signature or line drawing
keeping only the ink color of a scan for a one-color print
avoid: photos with soft, gradient or busy backgrounds: color matching leaves halos; cut out with a vector clipping path (PowerClip) or mask in PHOTO-PAINT instead
expecting the menu command to mask anything: it only toggles the docker, the masking happens on Apply
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("6268eac5-0cf7-4d43-a20a-aacc50b04562") only toggles the docker's visibility (it is a check button bound to the docker). The harvest records no object-model call that applies a color mask.

review.changes: none

cards.name: Break Link
cards.summary: Embeds an externally linked bitmap into the document, so the drawing no longer depends on the outside file. The image looks the same; only where its pixels live changes.
use_for: packaging a .cdr for a client or print shop so no linked image goes missing
freezing a linked photo before the source file is moved, renamed or edited
avoid: files that must keep picking up edits to the source image: keep the link and use Update from Link
very large linked images when file size matters: embedding stores the image data inside the .cdr, so the file grows
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("4917fa89-5d27-40d3-85d3-a7fba5df93ed"). Object-model equivalent (unverified): ActiveShape.Bitmap.ResolveLink (check ActiveShape.Bitmap.ExternallyLinked first). Disabled in every harvest state: it needs an externally linked bitmap selected.

review.changes: avoid: dropped the unsupported 'grows by the full image size' figure

cards.name: Line Drawing
cards.summary: Centerline trace with the Line Drawing preset: converts a black-and-white sketch into unfilled curves that run down the middle of each drawn line (strokes with an outline width) rather than filled outline shapes.
cards.how: Opens PowerTRACE with this preset loaded. Choices that matter: Detail, Smoothing and Corner smoothness sliders; Remove background (detect automatically or pick a color, optionally from the entire image); Merge adjacent objects of the same color, Remove object overlap, Group objects by color; Delete original image; on the Colors tab the color mode and number of colors. Compare before/after in the preview and read the curve / node / color counts before OK. Centerline traces produce stroked, unfilled curves, so line width is set by the outline, not by the traced shape.
use_for: turning a scanned pencil or ink sketch into editable stroked vector lines
hand-drawn line illustrations that need uniform, re-styleable stroke widths
preparing sketches for plotters, cutters or engravers that follow single paths
avoid: a low-resolution or heavily compressed source: clean it first (Resample up, Remove JPEG Artifacts) or the trace inherits the noise

losing or doubling the original: Delete original image removes the bitmap (leave it off if you still need it); with it off the traced group lands on top of the bitmap, so hide or move one before judging the trace
artwork whose line weight varies on purpose (brush lettering, ink washes): centerline gives every line one width; use Outline Trace > Line Art instead
precise mechanical drawings with straight edges: Centerline Trace > Technical Illustration is tuned for those
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("5B036050-31B4-475c-9BB5-695071514D8A") only opens the PowerTRACE dialog. Object-model route (unverified): Set ts = ActiveShape.Bitmap.Trace(cdrTraceLineDrawing) then adjust ts.Smoothing / ts.DetailLevelPercent / ts.SetColorCount and call ts.Finish (returns the traced ShapeRange).

review.changes: summary/how: 'single open curves / open paths' overclaimed (a drawn loop traces as a closed curve); now unfilled stroked curves; avoid: the 'keeping the original by accident' line contradicted its own advice (switch off Delete original to keep the bitmap); now covers both losing it and the trace sitting on top of it

redrawing technical diagrams so line widths can be standardised
single-path output for CNC, laser and plotter work from a line scan

cards.name: Crop Bitmap
cards.summary: Permanently discards the pixels of a bitmap that lie outside its clipping path (the boundary you shaped with the Shape tool), so the hidden area no longer travels in the file. What you see does not change; the bitmap's stored size shrinks.
use_for: slimming a file after cropping a large photo to a small area with the Shape tool
handing over artwork where hidden image areas must not be recoverable
avoid: a crop you may still want to adjust: leave the shaped boundary as is (non-destructive) or use a PowerClip frame
bitmaps whose boundary was never reshaped: there is nothing hidden to discard (behavior on an unshaped bitmap is unverified)

cards.name: Edit Bitmap
cards.summary: Opens the selected bitmap in Corel PHOTO-PAINT for pixel editing; when you save and close it there, the edited image replaces the original in the CorelDRAW document.
cards.how: Select one bitmap and choose the command; PHOTO-PAINT launches with the image. Retouch, then save and close (Finish editing) to send it back. The menu item is hidden in sandboxed (Store) builds of CorelDRAW.
use_for: retouching, cloning or healing a photo placed in a layout
pixel-level masking or painting that CorelDRAW's own bitmap tools cannot do
avoid: automated pipelines: it hands control to another application and waits for a person
simple tone or color fixes: Image Adjustment Lab or the Effects docker stay inside CorelDRAW
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("8c5788af-83c6-4ff7-bf11-ce603cf13c08") launches PHOTO-PAINT with the bitmap; finishing the edit is manual. No object-model call does the round trip.

cards.name: Image Adjustment Lab
cards.summary: Opens the Image Adjustment Lab, a one-stop photo correction dialog for the selected bitmap: automatic adjustment, white / black point pickers and sliders for temperature, tint, saturation, brightness, contrast, highlights, shadows and midtones, with a histogram, snapshots and a single, split or multi-view before / after preview.
cards.how: Start with Auto adjust or the white-point / black-point eyedroppers, then fine-tune Temperature and Tint (color cast), Brightness / Contrast, Highlights / Shadows / Midtones and Saturation. Take snapshots to compare versions, step back with Undo / Redo, then OK.
use_for: fixing color cast and exposure on product or event photos placed in a layout
quickly matching the warmth and contrast of several photos on one page
brightening shadows in a backlit portrait before printing
avoid: assuming the result is baked into the pixels, or that it stays editable, without checking: the lab is also offered as an editable effect in the Properties docker's effect list, and the harvest does not record which way this Bitmaps-menu route goes
heavy local retouching: use Edit Bitmap (PHOTO-PAINT)

cards.name: Auto Inflate Bitmap
cards.summary: Toggles the document preference that automatically enlarges a bitmap's canvas when a bitmap effect needs room beyond its edges (a blur, glow or distortion), so the effect is not clipped at the original border.
use_for: blurs, glows and distortions on cut-out images that must spread past the edge
switching it off when an effect must stay exactly inside the image frame
avoid: toggling blind from a script: each call flips the state, so know the current state first
precise control of the margin: use Manually Inflate Bitmap
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("aae3b767-8e13-4a6a-a4bc-011099dff7f2") flips the check button (two-way bound to the document preference AutoInflateBitmaps).

review.changes: none

cards.name: Manually Inflate Bitmap
cards.summary: Adds empty pixels around one selected embedded bitmap (to a new pixel size or by a percentage of the original) so later bitmap effects have room to extend past the original edges.
cards.how: Select exactly one embedded bitmap (not externally linked, not DeviceN color), then enter the new width and height in pixels or as a percentage of the original (it can only grow), optionally keeping the aspect ratio, and OK.
use_for: giving a cut-out product shot room for a soft glow or blur
padding an image before a distortion effect so the edges do not clip
avoid: externally linked bitmaps: the command is disabled; Break Link first
enlarging the picture content itself: use Resample
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("0a2d0181-85d8-4e8d-b0a5-92254e8d7dbc") only opens the dialog. Object-model equivalent (unverified): ActiveShape.Bitmap.Inflate Width, Height (units not recorded in the harvest).

review.changes: how/summary: there is no 'Inflate to' control (strings.xml); the dialog takes a new pixel width / height or a percentage, grow-only, with a keep-ratio option

cards.name: Black and White (1-bit)
cards.summary: Converts the selected bitmap to 1-bit black and white: every pixel becomes pure black or white, with a chosen conversion method (threshold line art, dither patterns or halftone screen) deciding how gray tones are simulated.
cards.how: Pick the conversion method: Line Art (hard threshold), Ordered, Jarvis, Stucki or Floyd-Steinberg dithering, Halftone (screen type, angle, line size) or Cardinality-distribution. Set Intensity / Threshold and watch the preview, then OK.
use_for: preparing scans for screen printing, rubber stamps, laser engraving or fax-style output
deliberate dither or halftone-dot looks for posters and zines
one-color line art that will be traced or colored by its fill
avoid: photos that need smooth tones: use Grayscale (8-bit)
anything you may need in color later: it throws away all tone information; convert a copy
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("256c8079-fd98-4d81-8553-ec2c5eaf758f") only opens the dialog. Object-model equivalent: Shape.Bitmap.ConvertToBW(RenderType, Intensity, Threshold, Halftone, Angle, Size), RenderType being cdrRenderLineArt 0 / Ordered 1 / Jarvis 2 / Stucki 3 / Floyd 4 / Halftone 5 / Cardinality 6 and Halftone cdrHalftoneSquare 0 / Round 1 / Line 2 / Cross 3. Plan runs 2026-10-15 (poster_print.line_engraving, poster_print.woodcut, poster_print.newsprint_halftone): ConvertToBW(5, 0, 128, 2, 45, 16), RenderType 5 with Halftone 2, gives a diagonal line screen whose line thickness follows the tone (engraving); ConvertToBW(0, 0, 112, 0, 0, 0), RenderType 0 with a threshold, gives solid black-or-paper two-tone line art (woodcut); ConvertToBW(5, 100, 128, 0, 45, 18) gives a dot screen (Size 0 gave a fine dither, 50 a coarse crosshatch, 30 was too coarse to read the picture).

review.changes: none

cards.name: CMYK Color (32-bit)
cards.summary: Converts the selected bitmap to CMYK color (4 channels, 32-bit) using the document's color management, so its colors are expressed in print inks; out-of-gamut RGB colors may look duller.
use_for: preparing photos for offset or digital print workflows that require CMYK images
checking how a bright RGB image will dull once printed
avoid: screen, web or social output: stay in RGB
converting before all edits are done: some effects and RGB-only tools work better before conversion; keep an RGB original
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("6ec34929-c4be-4f30-b12e-e10e5fde022f"). Object-model equivalent (unverified): ActiveShape.Bitmap.ConvertTo cdrCMYKColorImage.

review.changes: none

cards.name: Duotone (8-bit)
cards.summary: Converts the selected bitmap to a duotone: a grayscale image printed with one to four inks (monotone, duotone, tritone, quadtone), each ink's spread shaped by its own tone curve, giving a tinted, two-color-print look.
cards.how: Choose the type (Monotone, Duotone, Tritone, Quadtone), pick an ink color (often a spot color) for each, shape each ink's curve, and set overprint options; preview, then OK.
use_for: two-color print jobs with a brand spot color plus black
warm sepia or cool cyan-black photo treatments for posters and covers
consistent tinted photo styling across a brochure
avoid: full-color output: duotone keeps only one tone channel
a quick tint on screen only: a lens or tint effect is faster and stays editable

cards.name: Grayscale (8-bit)
cards.summary: Converts the selected bitmap to 8-bit grayscale (256 gray levels), discarding all color.

reducing file size of images that will print in black only
avoid: a black-and-white look you may want to undo: it discards color permanently; use a non-destructive effect or convert a copy

cards.name: Lab Color (24-bit)

cards.name: Paletted (8-bit)
cards.summary: Converts the selected bitmap to an 8-bit paletted (indexed) image of at most 256 colors, chosen from a palette type, with optional dithering to fake the missing colors.

use_for: small GIF-style graphics or limited-palette web assets
posterized or retro low-color looks

avoid: photos for print: banding and dither noise; keep RGB or CMYK
smooth gradients: they band unless heavily dithered

photos and complex art: unpredictable node counts without a preview

cards.name: Remove JPEG Artifacts
cards.summary: Uses CorelDRAW's machine-learning model to clean JPEG compression damage (blocky tiles, ringing around edges, smeared color) from the selected bitmap, applied straight from the menu (the harvest records no dialog for it).
use_for: rescuing a client logo or photo that arrived as a heavily compressed JPEG
cleaning an image before tracing it so the trace does not follow block noise
upgrading web-grabbed images before enlarging them for print
avoid: clean, high-quality images: nothing to fix and fine texture may soften; on a clean photo it changed no pixel (plan runs 2026-10-15 (retouch_cleanup.jpeg_artifacts))
general sensor noise rather than compression blocks: use a noise-reduction effect
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("18ae168e-2d47-4321-804b-b260036861f1"). No object-model equivalent is known. Plan runs 2026-10-15 (retouch_cleanup.jpeg_artifacts): through InvokeItem it ran with no dialog and no error; on a clean photo it changed no pixel (mean change 0.01 of 255), but on a photo re-saved as JPEG at quality 10 it smoothed the 8x8 blocking and the ringing round edges (mean change 2.8 levels) and softened the picture a little.

review.changes: summary: dropped the '8x8' figure (not in the batch); the no-dialog claim now rests on the harvest's missing opens_dialog flag

cards.name: Resample
cards.summary: Changes the pixel dimensions and / or resolution of the selected bitmap, adding or removing pixels. When enlarging, machine-learning upsampling modes rebuild detail instead of just blurring it.
cards.how: Set width / height (in units or %) and horizontal / vertical resolution; keep Maintain aspect ratio and Identical values on for proportional changes. Pick the mode: Nearest neighbor (hard pixels), Bicubic (smooth), or, when upscaling, Illustration (flat art) or Photorealistic (photos), with a noise-reduction slider. Compare original and new size, then OK.
use_for: enlarging a small logo or photo for print with ML upsampling
downsampling oversized photos to the output resolution to shrink the file
setting a consistent ppi on all images in a layout
avoid: simply showing an image smaller on the page: scaling the object keeps the pixels; resample only to change file size or resolution
scripted ML upscales: the object-model Resample has no Illustration / Photorealistic switch
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("f85cb8c1-b2a5-4f20-becd-be4918557275") only opens the dialog. Object-model equivalent (unverified): ActiveShape.Bitmap.Resample Width, Height, AntiAlias:=True, ResolutionX, ResolutionY.

cards.name: Straighten Image
cards.summary: Opens the Straighten Image dialog to level a tilted photo: align a straightening bar with something that should be horizontal or vertical, fine-tune the rotation, correct perspective and lens distortion, then optionally crop away the slanted edges.
cards.how: Drag the straightening bar along a line in the photo (horizon, building edge) or type the angle; fine-tune rotation, horizontal / vertical perspective and distortion while watching the grid; tick Crop to remove the slanted edges (and resample to keep the size if offered), then OK.
use_for: leveling horizons in travel and real-estate photos
squaring up photographed documents, signs and products shot at a slight angle
fixing converging verticals in architecture shots before a layout
avoid: scans of several photos on one bed: crop and straighten them one by one first
large rotations: it is built for small tilt corrections; rotate the object for big turns

cards.name: Update from Link
cards.summary: Reloads an externally linked bitmap from its source file, so edits saved to that file show up in the drawing.
use_for: refreshing a linked photo after it was retouched in PHOTO-PAINT or Photoshop
keeping a layout in sync with product shots that are still being updated
avoid: embedded bitmaps: there is no link to update (the command is disabled)

a moved or renamed source file: the update reads the stored path, so put the file back or point the link at the new file first (scripted: ActiveShape.Bitmap.LinkFileName is writable in the typelib, unverified); the live 2024 menus have no Links and Bookmarks docker
